Yes — three past cases are recorded, all in autumn 2025, all under accounts explicitly filed as "Betreuerwechsel" (handover). But be warned: the CRM holds the *complaints* and one post-mortem line, and almost nothing about how we actually reacted.

## What happened

| Account | When | What the customer said |
|---|---|---|
| Reply Deutschland (Katrin Sommer, katrin.sommer@reply.test) | 18 Sep 2025, inbound email "Wechsel der Ansprechpartner" | "Der ständige Wechsel der Ansprechpartner ist für uns ein echtes Problem." |
| valantic AG | 4 Nov 2025, inbound email | "Nach dem Wechsel des Ansprechpartners kam fünf Tage lang keine Antwort." |
| Körber Digital | 4 Nov 2025, inbound email (identical wording) | same — five days of silence after the handover |

## How we reacted

Only one record exists: an internal note on Reply Deutschland, 3 Dec 2025, subject **"Post-mortem Betreuerwechsel"** — *"Der Kunde hat das im Oktober klar angesprochen; wir haben zu spät reagiert."*

Note the timeline it implies: the complaint arrived in September, the customer raised it again in October, and the post-mortem is dated December. No remediation action, task, call or reply is logged against any of the three accounts — and all three inbound emails still sit as **needs_reply**, unanswered on the record to this day. No follow-up commitments and no owner-change history are recorded either.

## What to be prepared for

1. **The gap, not the change, is what they complain about.** Two of three complaints are literally about response latency after the swap (five days), not about the new person.
2. **A second mention means it is already escalating.** Reply Deutschland said it twice before anyone wrote it down.
3. **Repeat handovers are the sore point.** "Der ständige Wechsel" — this customer had experienced more than one.

## What to learn / do differently

- Have the outgoing manager introduce the successor *before* the switch, in writing, with a named fallback contact.
- Commit to a response SLA for the first two to four weeks and put it on someone's task list, so a five-day gap cannot happen unnoticed.
- Log the handover on the account and diary a check-in at day 14 and day 30.

Two caveats worth your judgement: these three organizations are named "<Company> Betreuerwechsel" and are classified `prospect` with no deals — they look like case/scenario records rather than the live accounts, so treat names and figures accordingly. And the two November emails are word-for-word identical across valantic and Körber, which could be two real customers or one event recorded twice. Nothing is waiting in approvals, and I changed nothing.
